To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a 3D mapping algorithm for a MAV that runs in real-time and is accurate, and that we have proposed algorithms for self calibration and self exploration.

(1) we propose a real time, constant space complexity, scalable 3D occupancy map that is suitable for vision guided robots, (2) we propose a wall following algorithm that works well for MAVs, (3) we propose a frontier based exploration algorithm for a MAV, (4) we propose simultaneous exploration and coverage algorithm for a MAV and a mobile robot, (5) we propose unsupervised self calibration algorithms for multi sensor systems.

(1) a 3D mapping algorithm can be designed to work well for both indoor and outdoor scenes; (2) a 3d mapping algorithm that runs at high frame rates can be designed; (3) a 3 dimensional map can be built with constant memory usage; and (4) a 3-dimensional map can be built that scales well to large scenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of algorithms that enable full autonomy for vision guided robots.
the development of algorithms that enable full autonomy for a mobile robot equipped with a forward-looking stereo camera.
the design and development of algorithms that enable vision guided robots to operate autonomously in unknown environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed work has contributed toward the goal of fully autonomous robots by providing solutions to some of the fundamental building blocks for full autonomy: self calibration, 3D mapping, and self exploration.
this thesis contributes to the development of autonomous robots by proposing a number of algorithms for self calibration, 3D mapping, exploration, and high level robot behaviors.
this work contributes to the vision based robot autonomy problem in two main ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed algorithms for self calibration, 3D mapping, and exploration that run on board a MAV.
we propose a 3 dimensional occupancy mapping algorithm that is fast enough to be used in a real time setting and is robust enough to be used on a MAV platform.

we have made progress in several directions toward full autonomy for vision guided robots: we have proposed a 3D mapping algorithm that runs fast and is robust to noise and occlusions, we have demonstrated wall following and frontier exploration behaviors, we have proposed a simultaneous exploration and coverage algorithm, and we have proposed self calibration algorithms for multiple monocular and stereo cameras.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of efficient algorithms for 3D reconstruction, accurate calibration, and efficient exploration can lead to a fully autonomous robot.
the combination of accurate perception and high level behaviors can lead to full autonomy for vision guided robots.
full autonomy is achievable in real world environments with a single forward looking stereo camera.
